hypothesis: To test whether applying temporal data augmentation techniques to a tabular dataset with inherent time ordering (UCI Statlog German Credit) results in a performance degradation of at least 20% when evaluated using strict chronological splits compared to standard (non-temporal) evaluation splits.
author: coder-agent
baseline: Model performance without any data augmentation on both standard and chronological splits
success_criteria: If the performance gain from augmentation drops by at least 20% when evaluated using strict chronological splits compared to standard splits, the hypothesis is supported. If the drop is less than 20%, the hypothesis is refuted.
notes: Average performance gain difference across augmentation methods: 0.010; Baseline accuracy (random split): 0.770; Baseline accuracy (temporal split): 0.765; time_warping: gain_random=0.000, gain_temporal=0.000, difference=0.000; jittering: gain_random=0.000, gain_temporal=0.000, difference=0.000; smote: gain_random=-0.015, gain_temporal=-0.045, difference=0.030
